 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Sri. Nanjappa .K. who met with road traffic accident.

2. That on 27-11-2023 at about 3-50 p.m., Nanjappa .K. was riding his TVS XL Moped bearing Reg.No.KA-07-EC-5098 on Bethamangala - Kolar road, Kolar District and when he reached near Kotiganahalli village gate, at that time the rider of TVS Apache motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-7-ED-9228 came from behind i.e., from Bethamangala in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the TVS XL moped, result of which, Nanjappa .K. fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to R.L. Jalappa hospital, Kolar wherein he succumbed to the injuries on 30-11-2023 at about 3-00 pm during the course of treatment.
So far, the petitioners have spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- towards Medicines, transportation of dead body, funeral obsequies expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, Nanjappa .K. was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 65 years.
He was Agriculturist by profession and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
Due to the sudden death of deceased, petitioners have suffered mental agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. On service of notice, the Respondent no.1 appeared through his counsel but he did file written statement.
5. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.2 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex- parte.

sentences.text: 6. The Respondent no.3/the Insurer of TVS Apache motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-7/ED-9228 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.3 has contended that the rider of the insured vehicle was not holding driving license and the said vehicle was not having FC and RC and that there was no nexus between the injury and death and that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and the petitioner in collision with the jurisdictional police has created false record and lodged false complaint to get compensation.

It is further contended that the accident in question has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the deceased, as he was riding the motorcycle without wearing helmet, without possessing valid driving license and rode the vehicle in rash a and negligent manner and dashed to the insured vehicle.

7. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, Sri.Nanjappa .K. was died on account of accident took place on 27-11-2023 at about 3.50 p.m., on Bethamangala - Kolar road, near Kotiganahalli village gate, Kolar Taluk and District, due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of TVS Apache motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-7-ED-9228?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
8.

On the other hand, the respondent no.1 got examined himself as RW.1.
9. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and respondent no.3 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

10. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;

In order to prove the petition averments, the petitioner no.1 who is the wife of deceased got examined herself as Pw1 and produced in all 12 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.P9 are police documents i.e., F.I.R with complaint, Police Memo with 2nd complaint copy, Spot mahazar, Spot Sketch, IMV report, Inquest report, PM report, Charge sheet and Death summary etc., are the material documents to prove the present point.
13.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Srikanth K son of the deceased, case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No.584/2023 of Kolar Rural Police for the offence punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.

The Investigation officer after completion of investigation has filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 304(A) of IPC.
14.

The learned counsel for respondent no.3 during the course of argument has vehemently submitted that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the deceased as the deceased had taken the vehicle towards right side result of which it hit to the offending vehicle.
Hence according to the learned counsel for respondent no.3, the deceased too has contributed negligence.

15. In the light of the submission made by the learned counsel for respondent no.3, if the complaint and other police records are perused, it discloses that at the time of accident the deceased was proceeding in Bethamangala - Kolar main road towards Kolar and offending vehicle which came from same direction hit to the vehicle of the deceased on its rear side.
The respondent no.3 has examined the driver of the offending vehicle as RW.1.

The RW.1 has deposed that while he was proceeding in the said road, the deceased who was proceeding in the two wheeler ahead of the offending vehicle took his vehicle towards right side and hit to the offending vehicle.

Though RW.1 who is the driver of the offending vehicle has stated that the accident in question has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the deceased but admittedly he has not lodged any complaint against the deceased.
The RW.1 has admitted the rough sketch and spot of accident shown in the rough sketch.
Admittedly there is no turn towards right side.
Hence the question of deceased taking the vehicle towards right side would not arise.
Admittedly on the basis of the compliant lodged against the RW.1, case has been registered against the PW.1 and after investigation charge sheet was filed against him.
Neither the owner nor the driver of the offending vehicle have challenged the charge sheet.
The spot mahazar and rough sketch clearly discloses the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Had the driver of the offending vehicle maintained minimum distance between the two vehicles, this accident would not have occurred.
Hence, the materials placed on record proves the issue no.1.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:
After considering the materials placed on record and the submission made by the learned respective counsels, it can be said that the deceased was died in the road traffic accident.
In the Ex.P11 - Aadhar card, the date of birth of deceased is shown as 06-07-1950.
Hence it can be Rathnamma vs Ashok V on 3 November, 2025

4 gathered that as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 73 years.
17. So far as the avocation and income of the deceased, as per the case of petitioners, deceased was Agriculturist by profession and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.
The petitioners have produced RTC's extracts pertaining to the property at Ex.P10 which stands in the name of deceased.
Hence, it cannot be ruled out that the deceased was doing agricultural work and earning income.
Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.
Since accident has occurred in the year 2023, the court has to consider the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,000/- per month.
18. The petitioners contended that the petitioner No.1 being the wife and petitioner no.2 being the son are the dependents of the deceased.
As per the own evidence of the PW.1, petitioner no.2 is teacher by profession and he is aged about 40 years.
Hence, though the petitioner no.2 is the legal representative of the deceased, but he is not the dependent of the deceased.
But the petitioner no.1 being the wife of the deceased is the dependent of the deceased.

19. Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had wife and she alone is the dependant of the deceased, hence, 1/3rd of the annual income is to be deducted towards personal expenses and remaining 2/3rd is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.
20. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors / Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: where in it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospects of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40%
of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, an addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
Hence in the instant case as the deceased was 73 years no future prospect can be considered.
21. Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.16,000/-, out of it if 1/3rd is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.10,666/-
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group for over 65 year is '5'.
Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.6,39,960/- (Rs.10,666 x 5 x 12 = 6,39,960/-).
22. Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner no.1 lost her husband and petitioner No.2 lost his father.

So far as quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium,
towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

23. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.
Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.
24. The PW.1 has deposed that they have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses for the treatment of deceased.
The petitioners have produced 6 medical bills amounting to Rs.58,057/- as per Ex.P12.
The learned counsel for respondents have not disputed the genuiness of medical bills.
As such petitioners are entitled for Rs.58,057/- under the head medical expenses.

25. In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
1 Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150-00 2
Transportation
and funeral Rs. 18,150-00 expenses
3 Loss of spousal consortium, Rs. 96,800-00 parental consortium (Rs.48,400X2) 4 Loss of Dependency Rs. 6,39,960-00 5

Medical bills Rs. 58,057-00 TOTAL Rs.
8,31,117/-
Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.8,31,117/- and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
26. As regarding liability is concerned, in view of the finding on issue No.2 there is liability on the part of the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
27. Issue No.3:- In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER  The claim petition filed by the petitioners are hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.8,31,117 + cost of Rs.2000/- imposed vide order on IA No.III and IV.
In all the petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.8,33,117/- (Rupees Eight Lakh Thirty Three Thousand One Hundred Seventeen only).
